lede: Both datasets collapse to one shape. On digits the losses barely move and the logged spread is already tiny. On Fashion the generator loss climbs, the training spread stays large, and the scored grid is one shirt.
title: Vanilla GAN
question: Do the generator and discriminator stay stable, and do the samples cover more than one mode?
process: Generator maps noise through an MLP that ends in tanh, so a sample lies in [−1, 1]. Discriminator maps an image to one probability. The loss is binary cross-entropy, criterion in the training step.
One discriminator step scores a real batch against a label of 1 and a generated batch against a label of 0:
The generator step uses the same fake batch and a label of 1, so D(G(z)) is pushed toward 1:
The loop takes one discriminator step and then two generator steps. There is no likelihood.

On 400 images per class for 40 epochs, digits eval losses stay near 1.40 and 0.68 and the grid is one stroke (sample std 0.0134). Fashion eval D falls to 0.20, eval G rises to 3.43, and the scored grid is one shirt.

The score file records sample std 0.0413 against real std 0.531, mode_collapse true, and every cell is the same shirt. The training log’s spread stayed large, so that series alone misses the collapse.

reflection.worked: Measured: both runs wrote 40 epochs of loss and a grid every epoch. The collapse flag matches the pictures: one stroke on digits, one shirt on Fashion.
reflection.unexpected: Measured: digits eval losses stay near 1.40 and 0.68 while sample std ends at 0.012, matching the score file’s 0.0134. Fashion eval D falls to 0.20 and eval G rises to 3.43, but logged std ends at 0.641 while the scored batch is 0.041.
reflection.why: Measured: the slice is 400 images per class, and the two stds are the same statistic on different noise draws. On Fashion those draws disagree. Guess: vanilla BCE gives the generator no class to cover, so one image that still fools the discriminator wins.
reflection.improve: Read the grid and the scored sample std beside the loss. The class-conditional run is the control that stops this collapse. On Fashion, where generator loss runs away, take a smaller discriminator step.
